sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the M.V. Act"), against the common judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge & J.M.F.C. & MACT, Kollegala (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the Tribunal"), dated 09.07.2020 in M.V.C.No.434/2018, seeking enhancement of compensation.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant.
Learned counsel for the respondent remained absent.
3. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties before the Tribunal is retained.

4. The case of the claimant who was the petitioner in the Tribunal is that, he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation of a sum of `25,00,000/- with interest at 18% per annum, on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 13.08.2018 at about 12:30 p.m.
5.

It is alleged that on 13.08.2018 at about 12:30 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a Motor Bike bearing registration No.KA-10/U-2383 towards Noor Mohalla,
Kollegala, and the rider was riding the said Bike slowly and cautiously, the driver of a KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-10/F-0256 drove the said Bus in a rash and negligent manner, in high speed, so as NC: 2024:KHC:20851 to endanger human life and hit the Motor Bike from behind.

On account of the accident, both the petitioner, being the pillion rider and also the rider fell down along Mubarakbege vs Divisional Controller on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12286492/
2 with the motor bike and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to the Government Hospital, Kollegala and treated as an in-patient.

The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus.
6.

In response to the notice served upon the respondent, the respondent-KSRTC appeared before the Tribunal and filed its Statement of Objections, denying the entire case of the petitioner regarding name, age, address, income and occupation of the petitioner as false for want of knowledge.
It further denied the occurrence of the accident, involvement of the KSRTC Bus and the rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus by its driver.

It also stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner was highly excessive and without any basis and that in the event of award of any compensation, the rate of interest NC: 2024:KHC:20851 may not exceed 6% p.a.
It also sought permission to invoke Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
Finally, it prayed that it is not liable to indemnify the petitioner and that the claim petition filed by the petitioner may be dismissed with costs.
7. Based upon the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal framed the following issues for its consideration.

1. Whether the petitioner proves that he is the victim of the Motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA- 10F-0256 on 13.08.2018 at about 12:30 P.M.(Noon) near KSRTC Depot, Kollegala Town within the limits of Kollegala Town Police Station and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to get compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and as against whom?
3.
Whether the respondent proves that it is not liable to pay compensation as pleaded in its objections?

4. What order or Award?
NC: 2024:KHC:20851 8.

To prove his case, the claimant/petitioner (appellant herein) got himself examined as PW-2 and the rider of the Motor Bike also got himself examined as PW-1, and they got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-9.
On behalf of the respondent-KSRTC, one Sri.K.L. Ashok, the Manager of the KSRTC was examined as RW-1 and no documents were got marked from their side.

However, one Dr.M. Rajashekar was examined through Court Commission as CW-1 and through him, four documents were got marked from Exs.C-1 to C-4.
9.

After hearing the arguments of the parties and going through the entire material placed before it,
the Tribunal, by answering issue No.1, in the affirmative, issue No.2, partly in the affirmative, issue No.3, in the negative and issue No.4, as per the final order, allowed the claim petition in part by granting the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:

during laid up period 10,000-00
4 Loss of future income 2,16,000-00  5 Loss of amenities 5,000-00  Total 2,40,000-00 10.

The Tribunal awarded compensation of a sum of `2,40,000/- with interest at the rate of `6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation of the entire amount, holding the respondent- KSRTC liable to pay the said compensation.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, on the ground that it is inadequate, the petitioner has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
11. Learned counsel for the petitioner strenuously contended that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under all the heads is meagre.
He submitted that the petitioner has suffered from reduced mobility and pain.
The Doctor (CW-1) has opined that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability at 45% in respect of left NC: 2024:KHC:20851 leg.
But the Tribunal has considered the permanent disability at only 10% which is less than 1/3rd of 45% and it ought to have been assessed at least at 15%.

Learned counsel further contended that, prior to the occurrence of the accident, the petitioner was doing gas welding work and earning a sum of `15,000/- per month, but after the accident and the injuries sustained, he is unable to do any type of work.

Even in the absence of proof of the income,
the Tribunal ought to have considered the notional income as considered in the Lok Adalaths.
For the accident occurred in the year 2018, the Lok Adalaths were assessing the notional income at a sum of `12,500/- per month.
Thus, assessing the income of the petitioner at only `10,000/- per month is very much on the lower side, considering the year of accident and the age and avocation of the petitioner.
Therefore, the notional income is required to be re-assessed by this Court.
NC: 2024:KHC:20851 Learned counsel further submitted that, the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of `5,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and was admitted as an in-patient in the Hospital for a period of twelve (12) days.

A sum of `4,000/-
awarded towards food, attendant charges and conveyance is very much on the lower side and is required to be enhanced reasonably.
Learned counsel further submitted that the compensation awarded towards loss of amenities in life is also on the lower side and required to be enhanced reasonably.

sentences.text: Learned counsel specifically submitted that the Tribunal has failed to award any compensation towards medical expenses, observing that the petitioner has taken treatment in the Government Hospital, free of cost.
Even in the Government Hospital, the petitioner has spent some sum towards incidental and other expenses.
Therefore, reasonable compensation may be awarded towards - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:20851 medical expenses.

Even though the Doctor has opined that the petitioner is required to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants by incurring `10,000/- to `15,000/-,
the Tribunal has failed to award any sum towards future medical expenses.
Therefore, just and reasonable compensation be awarded towards medical expenses and towards future medical expenses.

Thus, he prayed to award reasonable compensation by modifying the impugned judgment and award passed by Tribunal.
12.
Learned counsel for the respondent -KSRTC has not contested the matter.

13. After hearing the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner, the only point that arise for my consideration is, Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is very meagre and - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:20851 the same is liable to be enhanced reasonably?

If so, to what amount?
14.
After going through the Tribunal records, it is not in dispute that the accident has occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus.
The respondent-KSRTC has not challenged the award, except denying the averments made in the claim petition by filing the statement of objections and leading evidence before the Tribunal.
Hence, the liability fastened on the respondent-KSRTC is not disputed.
Thus, the only question that remains for consideration is about the quantification of the compensation, which, according to the claimant/petitioner is very meagre.
15. It can be seen that the Tribunal has awarded compensation of a sum of `5,000/- towards pain and sufferings.

Due to the accident, the petitioner has sustained fracture of left tibia - middle 1/3 displacement - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:20851 apart from a cut wound on the left leg measuring about 7x3 cms. bone deep,
an abrasion wound over the right forehead and an abrasion wound over the right elbow.
The Doctor has opined that the said injures are grievous in nature.

It is also stated that the petitioner has Mubarakbege vs Divisional Controller on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12286492/
5 undergone a surgery for implants.

entities.text: Mubarakbege vs Divisional Controller on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has taken treatment as an in- patient for a period of twelve days and also as an out- patient in the OPD.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained and age and avocation of the petitioner, I am of the view that a sum of `5,000/- awarded by Tribunal is very much on the lower side and liable to be enhanced reasonably.
Accordingly, I propose to award a sum of `40,000/- towards pain and sufferings as against a sum of `5,000/- awarded by Tribunal.
16. As regards food, nourishment expenses and attendant charges, the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of `4,000/-.
The petitioner has taken treatment as an in- patient for a period of 12 days and thereafter as an out- patient also.
During this period, he must have spent some - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:20851 sum towards conveyance, nourishing food and attendant charges.
But the compensation awarded by Tribunal at `4,000/- is very much on the lower side.

Therefore,
considering the duration of treatment undergone by the petitioner, both as an in-patient and also as an out- patient, I deem it fit and proper to award a sum of `15,000/- under the said head as against `4,000/- awarded by Tribunal.
17. As regards the compensation awarded towards loss of amenities, it is pertinent to note that, the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of `5,000/-.
The same is on the lower side for the reason that the petitioner has suffered a fracture injury and undergone a surgery for insertion of implants.
He was suffering from pain and swelling in fracture side and finding difficulty in climbing staircase and standing.
He was suffering from reduced movement in left knee and ankle.
On account of all these injuries, definitely he would be deprived of comforts and amenities in his future life.

Therefore, I propose to award a sum of - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:20851 `20,000/- towards loss of amenities in life as against a sum of `5,000/-
awarded by Tribunal.

18. As regards the compensation awarded towards loss of future earning capacity on account of permanent disability of the petitioner, it can be seen that the Doctor(CW-1) in his evidence has stated that the petitioner sustained fracture of middle 1/3d displacement, a cut wound on left leg measuring 7x3 cms. bone deep, abrasion wound over right forehead, abrasion wound over right elbow.
He has stated that the petitioner also underwent a surgery and implants were inserted.
He also stated that the petitioner was suffering from reduced movement in left knee and ankle.

Thus,
the Doctor assessed the permanent functional disability at 45% in respect of left leg.
1/3rd of the same would be the permanent disability towards whole body, which comes to 15%.
Thus, I propose to consider 15% permanent disability as against 10% assessed by the Tribunal.

- 15 - Mubarakbege vs Divisional Controller on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12286492/

sentences.text: So far as assessing notional income of the petitioner is concerned, it can be seen that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was doing Gas Welding work and earning a sum of `15,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any proper material to prove the said income.
In the absence of any evidence, either oral or documentary, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the petitioner by considering the Minimum Wages Rules under MNERGA at `10,000/- per month.

But considering the year of accident, age and avocation of the petitioner and also the notional income usually followed by the Lok Adalaths, I propose to re-assess the notional monthly income of the petitioner at a sum of `12,500/- as against `10,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
The petitioner has claimed that he was aged about 21 years in his claim petition.
But, the Wound Certificate (Ex.P-9) shows the age of the petitioner as 19 years.
In the other medical records also, the age of the injured petitioner is shown as 19 years.
But, in the absence of - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:20851 proper material in support of the age of the petitioner, the Tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 20 years.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, I find it just and proper and retain the same.
As already stated, the age of the petitioner is considered as 20 years at the time of the accident.

For the said age, the proper multiplier applicable as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs.Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in AIR 2009 SUPREME COURT 3104, is '18'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs.Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in AIR 2009 SUPREME COURT 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, taking the monthly income at `12,500/-, disability at 15%
and multiplier of '18', the compensation towards loss of future income on account of disability comes to `4,05,000/- (i.e. `12,500/- x 12 x 18 x 15%) .
Accordingly, the same is awarded as against `2,16,000/- awarded by Tribunal.

19. In so far as the compensation awarded towards loss of income during laid up period is concerned, it can be - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:20851 seen that, on account of the fracture injury and other injuries sustained in the road traffic accident, the petitioner was admitted to the Hospital on 13.08.2018 and took treatment for a period of 12 days as an in-patient.
Thereafter, he has taken follow-up treatment also in the OPD.
The Tribunal has considered the loss of income only for one month.

Considering the fracture injury and other injuries and also the fact that he underwent a surgery for implants, I am of the view that he must have been away from his work at least for a period of three months.
Thus, considering his income at `12,500/- per month, a sum of `37,500/- (`12,500/- x 3 months) is awarded towards loss of income during laid up period instead of `10,000/- awarded by Tribunal.
20. Further, it can be seen that the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards medical expenses on the ground that the petitioner has taken treatment in the Government Hospital, free of cost.

The Doctor (CW-1) in his evidence has categorically stated that the petitioner is Mubarakbege vs Divisional Controller on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12286492/
7 - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:20851 required to undergo one more operation for removal of implants, by incurring `10,000/- to `15,000/-.
But the Tribunal has not awarded a single pie either towards medical expenses or towards future medical expenses.

Even though the petitioner is said to have taken treatment in a Government Hospital free of cost, still, he must have spent some money towards medical tests, lab reports, and other incidental expenses.

Thus, considering the nature of injuries, surgery already undergone for implants and also future surgery for removal of implants, I propose to award a sum of `20,000/- towards medical expenses as well as future medical expenses.
21. Barring the above, the claimant is not entitled for compensation under any other heads or for any modification or enhancement of compensation under any other existing heads.

Thus, the appellant is entitled for a modified compensation as tabulated below:

3 Loss of income during laid up period 37,500-00  for a period of 3 months @
 Rs.12,500/- p.m.
4 Loss of future income 4,05,000-00
5 Loss of amenities 20,000-00
6 Medical expenses and future medical 20,000-00  expenses  Total 5,37,500-00
The quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal at `2,40,000/- is enhanced by a sum of `2,97,500/-, thus taking the total compensation to a sum of `5,37,500/-.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
[i] The appeal filed by the petitioner (appellant herein) stands allowed in part;

[ii] The impugned common judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge &
J.M.F.C. & MACT, Kollegala dated 09.07.2020 - 20 - Mubarakbege vs Divisional Controller on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12286492/
8 NC: 2024:KHC:20851 passed in M.V.C.No.434/2018, in so far as petitioner is concerned, is hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded at `2,40,000/- is enhanced by a sum of `2,97,500/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Ninety Seven Thousand Five Hundred only), with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation, thus fixing the total compensation at `5,37,500/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Thirty Seven Thousand Five Hundred Only).
